text:
maya: FYI, after the driver roll (535.54 -> 536.12) a subset of nodes lost all MIG profiles and GPU UUIDs changed, pods requesting specific MIG sizes fail.
jordan: Which nodes? Driver/kernel versions?
maya: us-west1-gpu-03, us-west1-gpu-04, us-west1-gpu-09. Driver: 536.12, CUDA: 12.2, kernel: 5.18.0-62 on 03/04, 5.19.0-8 on 09. Quick nvidia-smi from one node:
```
# nvidia-smi -L
GPU 0: NVIDIA A100-SXM4-40GB (UUID: GPU-abc123...)
MIG: disabled
```
alan: :eyes: 'MIG: disabled' after a driver upgrade usually means the MIG-capable driver wasn't fully initialized or MIG state was lost. Was the MIG bootstrap run by the installer?
maya: installer ran via rollout job (infra-deploy), rebooted once. kubectl logs show errors on the device plugin:
```
E0902 15:12:21.123 deviceplugin.go:210] failed to create MIG device: MIG_DEVICE_CREATE_FAILED: UUID mismatch for GPU: GPU-def456... not found
```
sre-jen: Could be kernel module mismatch (driver vs installed kernel headers) or leftover udev links from the previous driver. Also check nvidia-modprobe and nvidia-persistenced status.
ops-bot: Driver rollout job infra/driver-upgrade-2026-03-12 completed on 12 nodes (job id: 7834). No automatic rollback.
jordan: Try reprobing modules rather than full rollback: sudo rmmod nvidia_uvm nvidia_drm nvidia; modprobe nvidia; systemctl restart nvidia-persistenced; then run `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=gpu_name,gpu_uuid,mig.mode --format=csv`.
maya: Ran that on 03 and 04, got mixed results. Node 03 shows MIG enabled after reprobe, node 04 still reports old UUIDs in /var/lib/nvidia/ and device plugin can't map them.
alan: If /var/lib/nvidia contains stale MIG UUID files the plugin can mis-read mapping. Try `rm -rf /var/lib/nvidia/*` (careful) and restart the device plugin. Also `nvidia-smi mig -lgc` to list GPU contexts.
maya: Did a safe cleanup + restart of kubelet + nvidia-device-plugin, then `nvidia-smi mig -lgi` produced correct profiles on 03 but 09 still failed with "GPU UUID mismatch".
jordan: 09 is the only node that upgraded kernel to 5.19 by the automated image update last night — that might be the kicker. Kernel/driver ABI mismatch can produce different hardware UUID presentation.
sre-jen: Agreed. For 09 we should rollback kernel to match the tested ABI or isolate it from the rollout. I'm going to pin that node and re-run the driver with `--kernel-module-only` disabled so it rebuilds modules.
maya: Quick patch: I reinstalled the driver with `./NVIDIA-Linux-x86_64-536.12.run --dkms` and rebooted — made no difference on 09.
alan: Another pattern: NCCL/NVML library versions mismatch with the kernel module can cause NVML to expose different device identifiers. Check `/var/log/nvidia-installer.log` and dmesg for modprobe warnings.
maya: dmesg showed "nvidia: GPU UUID collision detected, assigning new temporary UUID" on 09. So NVML assigned a new UUID at probe time, causing the device-plugin mapping to break.
jordan: Short-term remediation: recreate the MIG device mappings after driver probe using `nvidia-smi mig -cgi <profile>` (example: `nvidia-smi mig -cgi 19,19,30`), then restart device-plugin. Longer-term: stop the automated kernel bump in the driver rollout job and run a staging canary that validates `nvidia-smi -q` + device-plugin unit test.
maya: I'll open infra ticket and schedule rollback for node 09. Also adding a pre-deploy check: after driver install run `nvidia-smi -q | grep -A2 MIG` and fail the job if MIG disabled or UUID changed.
sre-jen: I'll add a remediation script that checks for stale /var/lib/nvidia/* and runs `nvidia-smi --mig-mode=1 && nvidia-smi mig -cgi` with a known-good profile matrix. Also add a note in runbook: if GPU reports temporary UUIDs, power-cycle host when safe.
maya: Thanks — saving logs and making the ticket now. I'll pin rollout and mark 09 for rollback. :thumbsup: 
jordan: Good plan. Follow up in the ticket with the dmesg snippet and installer log.
maya: Will do. Thanks everyone.
